evidence: Joint release of 0102 and 0103, signed by the owner (D-Eminence) in chat on 2026-11-02: "approve 0102 and 0103". Review references: the owner's chat request of 2026-11-02 (D-Eminence), "i need the access pin and emergency to work in demo account now and fill both patient and ehr with the informaton you filled in the demo video" (0102), and the owner's chat request of 2026-11-01 (D-Eminence), "fix the two dashboard errors now" (0103 for the admin Overview's "Organization applications: Your account does not have permission" for the platform super admin; the other error, Demo requests failing, is fixed in identity-api alone in this release, which renames its two demo-request audit actions to admin.demo-requests.list and admin.demo-request.status so that 0064's audit_platform_scope_ck accepts the platform rows; no schema change). ORDER: 0102 then 0103; 0103 uses nothing 0102 adds and 0102 relies on none of the four bodies 0103 replaces. runtime-grants.sql gains two blocks, each only a revoke from PUBLIC (0102: the three demo-story functions; 0103: the organization application gate). The runner stops at the first refusal, so a 0102 refusal on production (any header-query answer other than the required one) also holds back 0103 with nothing applied; the owner runs 0102's header query before signing. JOINT PROOF of this release on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 run as pgrun: upgrade of a 0101 database by the runner (plan 2 pending, dry run rolled back with neither applied, apply 0102 in 27 ms and 0103 in 19 ms, then 0 pending, a re-run 0 pending, each file again by hand answers already applied); fresh install 0001-0103 (104 files); roles bootstrapped and verified on both; all 77 database suites pass on both (75 existing, sealed-demo-story, platform-organization-applications); the staging schema upgrade rehearsal passed (baseline 102, integrated 104, declared 0102 and 0103). With the role rds_superuser present (0098 seeded during the 0001-0101 apply, then the owner's password resets): with cross_facility_orders_enabled off the header query answered orders_on false and the dry run and the apply both stopped with 0102: SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ORDERS_OFF, neither 0102 nor 0103 applied; with every answer as required the dry run rolled back (0 PINs after), the apply seeded {pins 2, charts, orders 6, audited 56, changed 20, renamed 10, profiles 4, registrationCases 4} and applied 0103, then 0 pending and the header query answered pins 2, story 71; a second call of the seed changed nothing; the 0103 suite passes on the seeded database. The identity-api change: tsc clean, jest 1857 of 1857. PART 1, 0102 (sealed demo story). Backward compatible: no table, column, index, constraint, policy, trigger or existing function changes; pg_dump --schema-only of a 0101 database before and after differs only by three new functions in schema identity and their comments, all owned by the applier and granted to no role (revoked from PUBLIC in the file and in runtime-grants.sql's 0102 block, which is only that revoke). No service calls them, so every image now running gives the same answers. WHAT IT DOES. identity.demo_story_install(pin_hash) (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp) fills the 0098 sealed demo tenant with the demo video's made-up story; identity.demo_story_context and identity.demo_story_lab_result are its helpers. It runs on Amazon RDS only (rds_superuser exists), as 0098's install does; everywhere else (CI, acceptance, rehearsals) nothing is seeded and the suite sealed-demo-story calls the seed with its own test hash. On production it: renames the ten demo patients (Adaeze Okafor, born 1991-03-04; Chinedu Okafor; Abubakar Bello, Halima Yusuf, Emeka Nwosu, Ngozi Eze, Musa Ibrahim, Funke Adebayo, Ifeanyi Okeke, Zainab Lawal; Health IDs unchanged), the two patient logins' display names, and the staff login's display name and staff name (Dr Tunde Bello), each only from 0098's own value; adds the hospital, HMO and health information the patient portal counts, where the patient saved none; stores the owner's PIN hash ($2a$12$, pgcrypto, the PIN in no file) as identity.set_my_patient_access_pin stores a PIN, for Patient One and Two where they have no PIN row, revoking no grant; writes, as the demo login's doctor membership at Demo Hospital through 0098's shares, Adaeze's completed visit six weeks before the apply and today's visit in progress (vitals, signed notes, diagnoses Z88.0, D50.9, B54, ferrous sulphate, artemether-lumefantrine, paracetamol, a malaria rapid test and a full blood count) and Chinedu checked in today; sends the six orders with ehr.send_order_route and accepts them with lab.accept_order_route and pharmacy.accept_order_route at Demo Laboratory and Demo Pharmacy; writes the Lab's steps to two entered results (not checked or released: lab.validate_result_governance needs a second person, and the demo has one login) and two dispensings (6 and 18 tablets), which complete those two routes; adds two Outreach campaigns and four registrations, not linked to the campaign (outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write, 0045, reads the campaign member FOR SHARE, which forced row-level security refuses an owner without BYPASSRLS because outreach.campaign_members has no UPDATE policy; the same check runs for outreach-api, so a live registration into a campaign may meet the same refusal: reported, not changed). Every row is demo (55000 SEALED_DEMO_STORY_NOT_DEMO otherwise). Refusals, each 55000 with nothing written: SEALED_DEMO_STORY_LOGINS_NOT_READY (the three demo logins not all active), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ORDERS_OFF (cross_facility_orders_enabled or cross_facility_route_access_enabled off), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_SHARE_MISSING (a 0098 share at Demo Hospital revoked), and, asked before any order command runs so the release never stops inside one, SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ROLE_MISSING (a demo membership inactive or a send or receive permission gone), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_DESTINATION_OFF (Demo Laboratory or Demo Pharmacy not eligible to receive, for example unlisted by support), SEALED_DEMO_STORY_PATIENT_RESTRICTED (Adaeze or Chinedu not active, without a Health ID, or with a deny directive naming a destination) and SEALED_DEMO_STORY_ORDER_LIMIT (the daily send, pair, open-order or wrong-patient limits); the Health IDs and attestation texts given to the commands are read from the database; 22023 SEALED_DEMO_STORY_PIN_HASH_INVALID for any hash but bcrypt cost 12. Once only: a second call changes nothing. Nothing is sent: the order notices (sent, accepted) are marked read in the same transaction, so no web push is due; no lab or pharmacy outbox row for results or dispensings, no identity outbox row, no delivery attempt; the accept commands queue LabWorkItemCreated and PharmacyWorkItemCreated integration events as for any order, which no notification workflow reads. Audit: one row of the migration's own per row written (actor system, provenance migration, source system hid-sealed-demo, correlation id 0102-sealed-demo-story, ids only, the PIN's with its cost and never the hash; 56 rows) and one story row with counts; no audit row names a patient or clinician; the order commands add their own 14 system rows. Preconditions (catalog reads, 55000/42501, nothing applied): 0001-0101 objects present, none of 0102's, 40 relied-on function bodies byte for byte (md5 of prosrc), the two profile tables' owner policies naming the applier, CREATE on schema identity. Locks: none up front; on production the seed takes ROW EXCLUSIVE on the tables it writes and row locks on ten patients, three accounts and one staff record until commit. Measured on throwaway PostgreSQL 16: apply 13 ms (functions only); the forced seed in one transaction about 1.1 s, also run whole as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (every schema, table and function reowned, the 0094 owner policies naming it), so every write passed the tables' forced row-level security, triggers and the 0098 seal guards, with the same 56 audit rows. Proven on throwaway PostgreSQL 16: fresh install 0001-0102 (103 files) and upgrade from 0101 (plan 1 pending, dry run rolls back, apply, then 0 pending; the file again answers 0102: already applied), roles bootstrapped and verified, every DB suite green on both, the new suite sealed-demo-story green (refusals, the owner's hash stored verbatim at cost 12 and accepted by pgcrypto without any PIN tried, the seed, row-level security reads by the EHR, Lab, Pharmacy and Outreach runtimes, nothing sent, the audit, idempotency, the PIN at Demo Hospital with the suite's own test PIN, break-glass on Abubakar Bello and Adaeze), the migration ledger, release contract and release-gate tests. Before signing, the owner runs the read-only query in the file's header on production: rds 1, active_logins 3, orders_on true, roles_ok true, hospital_shares 2, destinations_on true, patients_open true, limits_ok true, pins 0, story 0; any other answer is the matching named refusal, and the release would stop with nothing applied. Proven on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with the role rds_superuser present (so 0098 and 0102 seed as on production): with Demo Laboratory unlisted the header query answered destinations_on false and the dry run and apply both stopped with 0102: SEALED_DEMO_STORY_DESTINATION_OFF and nothing applied; with every answer as required the dry run rolled back and the apply seeded the story with the owner's hash (pins 2, orders 6, 56 audit rows), then 0 pending. PART 2, 0103 (platform organization applications; main 0067's gate fix on this branch's 0064 audit model). 0103 (platform organization applications; main 0067's gate fix on this branch's 0064 audit model) is backward compatible. WHAT CHANGES. Four existing SECURITY DEFINER functions get new bodies by CREATE OR REPLACE (signature, language, volatility, search_path, owner and ACL kept, checked after): identity.organization_application_admin_account(text) (0046's body; md5 4ce43509b97996cdbb5997dc18c8c400 before, 186eb4ca420749b8bdb324bdc843bc50 after), identity.admin_record_organization_cac_result (0056; 3b1aca8cd1a4854d465c5b300bc10aca before, 99aeaad4074f9d74c3f036817aedaeb6 after), identity.admin_approve_organization_application (0056; 532e5003f0d2084437c28c3706a95ecd before, 258e24e471d555b716dc0f57bab185e3 after) and identity.admin_reject_organization_application (0046; cd34d46405bc32eeef38a2108309991e before, 8f449d98d58cfffff2e74a3b776a2055 after). The gate: a platform-scoped call (no facility and no membership in the request context, as the Identity API's withPlatformTransaction sends for an administrator with no facility, and the account holds platform.admin.access) no longer needs identity.has_active_membership and is authorized by auth.account_has_platform_permission(actor, requested_permission) alone; every other call keeps exactly 0046's check (a session that names a facility or a membership still needs an active membership there); the account, correlation id and purpose rules are unchanged and the requested permission is still required of everyone; no permission is granted to anyone. The three writers: in a platform-scoped call the audit row is actor_type 'platform', action admin.organization-application.cac-verify, .approve or .reject, with facility, membership and organization null (approve keeps the new organization's id in details.organizationId), which 0064's audit_platform_scope_ck, audit_actor_facility_ck and audit_platform_authority accept; a facility-scoped call writes exactly today's row (actor_type 'staff', identity.organization.application.* actions, its facility, membership and organization). Without the writer change the CAC check, approval and rejection would still fail for the super admin once the list worked (audit_actor_facility_ck). Callers kept and pinned: admin_list_organization_applications, admin_get_organization_application and platform.consume_qoreid_quota ('application_cac'). runtime-grants.sql gains a 0103 block revoking the gate from PUBLIC (it has no EXECUTE for anyone but its owner); no grant, table, column, constraint, policy, role or permission changes; no row is touched. SERVICES: none; today's Identity API image sends the same calls in the same transactions. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0101 applied (0101's validate_dispensing body the marker); not applied yet; md5 of the four bodies, the three callers, platform.current_account_id, current_actor_subject, current_facility_id, current_membership_id, current_correlation_id, current_purpose_of_use, auth.account_id_for_subject, identity.has_active_membership, auth.account_has_platform_permission and audit.authorize_platform_event; the four functions' attributes; audit_actor_type_ck, audit_actor_facility_ck and audit_platform_scope_ck by definition and the audit_platform_authority trigger; one owner for the four, and the applier is it or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it. Nothing 0102 adds is used or required. LOCKS, measured with pg_locks before commit: ACCESS SHARE on schema identity and the language, the replaced pg_proc rows and the session's own temporary table and schema; no application table lock held to commit. Behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.organization_applications or audit.events the runner stopped after its 5 s lock timeout (5.1 s), nothing applied; behind ROW EXCLUSIVE on either, or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on auth.accounts, it applied in 0.1 s. Apply time 7-15 ms (execution_ms). PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 as pgrun: an upgrade of a 0101 database by the runner (plan, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending after, the file applied again answers 'already applied'), and a fresh install of 0001-0101 and 0103 in one run (103 migrations); the role bootstrap and its verification pass on both; all 76 database suites pass on both (75 existing and the new one); the new suite fails on the 0101 base. A NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner and a member login of it each apply 0103 (owner and ACLs kept) and the new suite passes on both; a role that is neither is refused with 42501. Negative copies stop with nothing applied: the gate's body changed, audit_platform_scope_ck dropped, the authority trigger disabled, audit.authorize_platform_event changed, the reject command's search_path changed or SECURITY INVOKER, has_active_membership changed, 0101 missing, the four functions under two owners. Mutants: 11 of 11 killed (the admin.access term dropped, the facility or membership term dropped, the requested permission skipped in platform scope, the membership check dropped, the writers' staff actor type, identity.* action or organization kept for platform rows, every row as platform, the organization missing from approve's details, reject's outcome changed). Today's Identity API code (OrganizationApplicationsService with the real DatabaseService transaction settings and IntegrationRuntimeService quota call, provider call stubbed) on a 0101 database answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for the super admin; on 0103 it lists, checks the CAC, approves and rejects, writing three platform audit rows. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/platform-organization-applications.integration.sql: the super admin lists, reads, reserves CAC quota, records a failed and a passed CAC check, approves and rejects, with platform audit rows; a facility admin's rows unchanged; refused (42501, no row, no audit, no quota): a platform account without platform.admin.access, a disabled account, an inactive membership, another account's membership, a facility without a membership and the reverse, no correlation id, another purpose, no purpose, an unknown subject; the identity reviewer lists but cannot read, check, reject or reserve quota.
